today.body:
Tiny promise (love):  
After I finish my lunch break, I will send one friendly, honest message to a person I met this week saying, “It was great meeting you, would you like to grab coffee sometime?”  
Floor version: type the short sentence and hit send in under 30 seconds.  
Why it works: a concrete, low‑effort outreach turns a pleasant memory into a real connection.

Learning from the world:  
Tippy shows that asking a simple, open‑ended question right after a greeting lets you hear ideas you might otherwise miss. When you listen first, you build trust and uncover quick improvements that benefit the whole team. Applying the same habit to dating means you’ll learn what matters to the other person, making the next step feel natural.

Español del día:  
**¿Qué una cosa podríamos cambiar para mejorar la inspección de hoy?** – “What one thing could we change to improve today’s inspection?”  
Use it right after logging into your computer each morning when you greet an inspector, or in a first‑date conversation to invite collaborative ideas.

Weather note: With a mild 63 °F high, a quick walk to the floor after lunch feels refreshing and helps you focus.

b.advice: Link the greeting to a concrete, already‑done cue: right after you click the computer’s login button (the trigger), say the exact phrase “Buenos días, ¿cómo va la línea hoy?” and then immediately follow with one specific question about today’s production (e.g., “¿Qué observaste en la línea ayer?”). Write the cue‑action pair on a sticky note on your monitor so the visual reminder is present at the moment of login. After you finish, tick a single box on a paper habit‑tracker labeled “Greeting done”. The visual cue, the tiny 30‑second script, and the immediate tick provide clear implementation intention, environmental prompt, and instant feedback, which together boost automatic execution even on a bad day.

t.lesson: After you log in, walk to the nearest inspector and say, “Buenos días, ¿cómo va la línea hoy?” then ask, “¿Qué una cosa podríamos cambiar para mejorar la inspección de hoy?” Listen fully before responding.
